title: Strict transform over the complement of the center
statement:
Let $X'\to X$ be the blow-up of a center $C\hookrightarrow X$. Over
$X\setminus C$, the strict transform is canonically the ordinary pullback.
This identification is compatible with the projection to the original
scheme.

proof.text:
This is exactly
[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-over-complement], applied to the ideal
defining $C$. The compatibility with the projection is part of that
canonical identification.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent ideal with
center $C=V(\mathcal I)$, let $b\colon X'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)\to X$
be the blow-up, and let $f\colon Y\to X$ be a morphism. Let
$\Omega\subseteq Y\times_XX'$ be the open subscheme lying over
$X\setminus C$ and let $\widetilde Y\hookrightarrow Y\times_XX'$ be the
strict transform of $f$ along the blow-up ([def-nagata-strict-transform]).
Then the part $\widetilde Y\times_{Y\times_XX'}\Omega$ of the strict
transform lying over $X\setminus C$, together with its projection to $Y$
and the map to $b^{-1}(X\setminus C)\xrightarrow{\sim}X\setminus C$, is a
fibre product of $f$ and the inclusion $X\setminus C\hookrightarrow X$.
Thus over $X\setminus C$ the strict transform is canonically
$Y\times_X(X\setminus C)$, compatibly with the projection to $Y$.

proof.text:
By [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] the blow-up restricts to an
isomorphism $b^{-1}(X\setminus C)\xrightarrow{\sim}X\setminus C$, so
[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-over-complement] shows that $\Omega$, with
its projection to $Y$ and the map to $X\setminus C$, is a fibre product of
$f$ and $X\setminus C\hookrightarrow X$. It remains to see that the strict
transform contains all of $\Omega$, i.e. that the projection
$\widetilde Y\times_{Y\times_XX'}\Omega\to\Omega$ is an isomorphism. This
projection is a closed immersion. Since $\widetilde Y$ is the
scheme-theoretic image ([def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]) of the open
immersion $j\colon\Omega\hookrightarrow Y\times_XX'$, its ideal is the
kernel ideal of $j$ ([lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc]), and the ideal
of the projection is the extension of that kernel ideal along $j$
([def-nagata-extended-ideal]). This extension is zero because
$j^\sharp$ restricted to $\Omega$ is the identity of $\mathcal O_\Omega$.
A closed immersion with zero ideal is an isomorphism, and transporting the
fibre square of $\Omega$ along it gives the claim.
